turns.speaker: user
turns.text: I've got about two thousand in savings and I can't decide where to keep it.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: I'll tell you all the choices first. Wait until I'm finished before you comment.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: I could leave it in my normal current account, which pays basically nothing but is easy to reach.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Or move it to a high interest savings account, which pays more but takes a day or two to withdraw.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Or put some into a simple index fund, which could grow more but can also go down.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Right, um, that's everything, I think. Your thoughts?

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: If this is your emergency money, the high interest savings account is the sweet spot, safe and still earning something. The index fund is better for money you won't need for years. Your current account is easy but your money just sits there.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Can I ask about something else? Somebody's trolley left a long scratch on my door at the supermarket.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Ugh, that's infuriating. Can you catch your fingernail in it, or is it just on the surface?

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Then it's through the clear coat but maybe not to bare metal. A touch up pen in your car's exact paint colour can hide it well.
